diagnostic_evidence.quote: These are just the Euler-Lagrange equations fulfilled by a minimizer of the energy $E$ on the space $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under the constraint $P_H(u_H^{\mathcal{L}}) \in \mathbb{S}$. Since the functional $E$ is quadratic, the precise normalization is not crucial.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that because $E$ is quadratic, the choice of normalization constraint is not crucial and that rescaling the minimizer $u_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under $\|P_H(u)\|_{L^2}=1$ yields the minimizer $\tilde{u}_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under the standard normalization $\|u\|_{L^2}=1$. This is mathematically false: $\|P_H(u)\|_{L^2}$ and $\|u\|_{L^2}$ are two distinct, non-proportional norms on $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$, since $\|u\|_{L^2}^2 = \|P_H u\|_{L^2}^2 + \|(I-P_H)u\|_{L^2}^2$ and the corrector $(I-P_H)u$ has a non-constant relative $L^2$-norm across $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$. Minimizing the quadratic energy $E(v)$ subject to $\|P_H v\|_{L^2}=1$ (which leads to the generalized eigenvalue problem $(u, v)_X = \lambda_H (P_H u, P_H v)_{L^2}$) and subject to $\|v\|_{L^2}=1$ (which leads to $(u, v)_X = \mu_H (u, v)_{L^2}$) yield different eigenvectors in general, so $u_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ and $\tilde{u}_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ are not proportional.

failure_location.quote: In particular, if $u_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ is a minimizer in $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under normalization $P_H(u_H^{\mathcal{L}}) \in \mathbb{S}$, then $\tilde{u}_H^{\mathcal{L}} := \tfrac{\| P_H(u_H^{\mathcal{L}}) \|_{L^2(\D)} }{ \| u_H^{\mathcal{L}} \|_{L^2(\D)} } u_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ is a minimizer in $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under the standard normalization $\tilde{u}_H^{\mathcal{L}} \in \mathbb{S}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the claim that $u_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ rescales to $\tilde{u}_H^{\mathcal{L}}$, and clarify that the fixed point of the collocation scheme minimizes $E$ on $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under the projected norm $\|P_H(u)\|_{L^2}=1$, which is a closely related but distinct LOD formulation from the standard Galerkin minimization in (2.14).
issues.overall_effect: The asserted equivalence between the limit of the metric-driven collocation scheme (Definition 2.2 / Conclusion 2.3) and the standard Ritz-Galerkin LOD minimizer (2.14) fails. The collocation scheme approximates a Petzoldt/saddle-point type discretization rather than the exact Galerkin minimizer (2.14).
issues.title: False claim that normalization under projected L2 norm is equivalent to standard L2 normalization
issues.why_classification: Theorem 2.5 independently analyzes the Galerkin minimizer (2.14) using established results from the literature and does not rely on the false proportionality. A routine local prose clarification restores consistency without affecting any theorem statement, proof, or convergence guarantee.
